inputs.original_text: Cuba’s communist system has left ordinary people without the property or money needed to rebuild their lives. A transition that lets wealthy diaspora buyers and foreign investors scoop up Cuban property at bargain prices would only replace one form of dispossession with another. Cuban families and local ownership must come first; a nation’s future should not be handed to whoever arrives with the deepest pockets.
inputs.modified_text: Cuba’s ordinary people shouldn’t be made to bear the cost of rebuilding while wealthy diaspora buyers and foreign investors turn hardship into a bargain-hunting opportunity. Replacing state control with a fire sale would not be justice; it would shift power to those with money. Any transition must protect Cuban families, workers, and local ownership, and give people a real say in their country’s future.

rationales.subtopic_drift: The modified text shifts emphasis toward fire-sale privatization, rebuilding costs, workers, and public participation, while the original foregrounds deprivation under the communist system and property dispossession.
rationales.entity_drift: The main actors remain ordinary Cubans, wealthy diaspora buyers, and foreign investors; workers are added, while the communist system is no longer explicitly named.
rationales.relation_drift: The original asserts that the communist system left people without resources and hypothesizes renewed dispossession through bargain property sales. The modified text instead recommends that people not bear rebuilding costs and describes a fire sale as shifting power to the wealthy.
rationales.contradiction_drift: The modified text contains no meaningful internal contradiction.
